upper_bound.quote: (standard; details omitted). In all cases $G_p$ is invariant. $\blacksquare$
upper_bound.witness: The whole content of the invariance obligation is the claim that for every positive integer t, (t | α and t | β) ⇺ (t | min(α,β) and t | |α-β|), and its proof is explicitly deferred ("details omitted"). What would have to be proved, for all cases, is: gcd(α,β) = gcd(min(α,β), |α-β|) covering α = β (where β' = 0 and one must use gcd(x,0) = x), α = 0 or β = 0, and the generic case, together with the deduction that the common divisors of the full 2026-tuple, hence G_p, are unchanged. The quoted passage asserts the equivalence and the invariance without any argument for any case.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Part (b) rests entirely on G_p being invariant; Step 4 derives v_p(M) = gcd(v_p(a_i)) solely from this omitted claim, so with the claim unproved the choice-independence of M is unsupported.

parsed.notes: Answer formula explicit and correct; move description and termination/exactly-one-survivor arguments are complete. The prime-wise gcd invariance, the core of (b), is asserted with "details omitted" and only backed by examples and computer checks.
